Further on the garrison outpatient clinic, the pensioners' residence, et cetera. Mr. Jasak, as I understand you, you did not have any personal knowledge, you did not take part in fighting in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take part in fighting in Mostar on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, according to the information that reached you on that day, if you can remember, are the references to localities where there was fighting correct?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to Ismet Hadziosmanovic's book. That is to say, document 3D3101. It says in -- further on: "Already around 11.00 concentrated infantry fire was heard at the locality of Mujaga Komadina's house, part of the former street Lenjinovo Staliste, Liska park, and the Rondo. Later on, it became obvious that these were maximum infantry breakthroughs by the 4th Corps. Roughly that's where they stayed, in that broader location. Heavy machine-guns continue to focus their fire on the Vranica building." Now my question, Mr. Jasak. Is it correct when it is asserted that the HVO attacked BH Army positions in the Vranica building?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, this information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, all these localities that we mentioned just now, are they to the west or east of that line of delineation or separation that was agreed upon on the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the localities are to the west of the agreed line of separation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Jasak, on that morning, the 9th of May, was General Petkovic the Chief of the Main Staff at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about when he arrived in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrive, to the best of my knowledge -- I mean, as far as I can remember, it was around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see him?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the first thing was that General Petkovic did when he arrived in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked to have Lasic and Pasalic called for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the second last name that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked to have Lasic and Pasalic called for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to where it was that General Petkovic had arrived from?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge as to where he had arrived from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know anything else about Mr. Petkovic's communications? Did he really manage to speak to Lasic and Pasalic? Did he meet up with them?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he met up with them or not and whether he talked to them or not. When the general arrived, I went to my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I've prepared two documents for you. Since my time is running very quickly, I'm not going to show them to you, but I'm going to refer to them. On the 8th of May, 1993, Ratko Mladic and Sefer Halilovic signed an agreement on an instance cease-fire. 4D1344 is the number of that document. Please have a look at that document. That is one of the documents that follows in your binder. Tell us, Mr. Jasak, did the VOS have any knowledge about the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Army of Republika Srpska agreeing on a cessation of all hostilities throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina as referred to in this agreement?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have such knowledge. I already told you about that previously when we were discussing Konjic. We did have some information to the effect that certain talks were being held since January and that they, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, were asking for this to be secured for them and that they would pay for certain amounts of weapons and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: As a military analyst, how would you interpret this document from which we can see that on the 8th of May, 1993, the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Army of Republika Srpska had agreed on a cessation of all hostilities throughout the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would interpret this document in the following way: that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina no longer intended to fight the Army of Republika Srpska and that they were turning to the creation of their own living environment at the detriment of their hitherto ally, that is to say, the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Jasak, on that day, the 9th of May, until when were you at the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there until the late evening hours, almost up until midnight.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How would you describe the intensity of the fighting in the course of the evening? Was it of the same intensity as that morning or was it considerably less?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was considerably less. Evidently the night-time conditions had contributed to decreasing the intensity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 10th of May. On the 10th of May, did you go to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, in the morning. I was on duty that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That morning, did General Petkovic go to the Main Staff in?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did arrive there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what did he do that morning in the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He arrived in his office in the morning. At around 9.00 a.m. he received a call from Mr. Boban's office, and he said he was going to Grude, that they were going to have a meeting between Mr. Boban and Mr. Izetbegovic concerning a cease-fire and that he had to provide some elements of information for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, we'll have to repeat the last part of the question because it was misinterpreted. It appears that there was a meeting. What was actually agreed on?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was agreed on was that the elements for a cease-fire agreement were to be discussed and that General Petkovic had to provide some elements needed for that agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, let me come back to document 4D1344, document which I see for the first time, and I don't recall having seen this document previously. It's dated 8th of May; that's an important date. This is a document which is signed by Halilovic and Mladic. However, this document is signed under the auspices of General Morillon. What does this document say? Well, first HV -- the HVO is not a part in this document. This document states that for the restoration of peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina a consensus is reached between the two parties. Cease-fire as of noon on the 9th of May. Well, I take it, and I have no evidence for that, that General Halilovic must have afterwards called all of the commanders of the corps, the 1st Corps, the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Corps and particularly Pasalic to tell him, Look, Arif, I want to announce you that on the 9th of May you need to stop firing. It's an assumption. And that the agreement will have to be implemented because UNPROFOR is a part to it, a part to this agreement. And so, with this information, Pasalic arrives. And Pasalic, for whatever reason, could have, in the conditional tense, could have thought, Well, we'll attack and we'll stop everything at noon, but in the meantime we will have made some headway. And this could explain the thesis of the Defence about the BH Army's attack. I mean, that's a question which came to my mind from this document. Now, you at the time were in military intelligence. Had you learned that there had been an agreement between your "enemy," i.e., the Serbs, and your "friends," the BH Army? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Military Intelligence Service, we knew that they had reached an agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you found out before the 9th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the 9th of May. We know it was signed on the 8th, but we knew that they had discussed it previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. That's what I wanted to check.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, we're -- we've now reach the 10th of May. In the morning General Petkovic set out for Grude to see Mate Boban in order to agree on a cease-fire with Alija Izetbegovic. Let's look at 4D456 and 4D457. These are orders issued by Mato Boban and Alija Izetbegovic, dated the 10th of May, 1993. The text is almost identical. And this order orders a cessation of hostilities between the BH Army and the HVO; and Sefer Halilovic and Milivoj Petkovic are tasked with arranging a meeting to agree on all the details for the implementation of this agreement. My question is as follows, Mr. Jasak: As the person on duty in the Main Staff, were you aware of how General Petkovic's activities in Grude ended and that a cease-fire agreement had been reached?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that it had been agreed on. The order was issued by Mato Boban and Alija Izetbegovic to start a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, tell us, do you know where General Petkovic went then?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, the general did not return to the Main Staff. He told us that the following day he had to go to Kiseljak to meet General Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is under seal, so please take care. It's P2461. It's an UNPROFOR report. On page 6 in Croatian, which is part 13, the Neretva River valley, it says that Generals Halilovic and Petkovic had a meeting on the 11th and reached an agreement, and this took place in Kiseljak. They reached an agreement to tour the town of Mostar together on the same day. Mr. Jasak, did you know that General Petkovic actually did meet General Halilovic in Kiseljak on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the report it goes on to say that on the 11th of May, at 1830 hours, Generals Halilovic and Petkovic, accompanied by General Morillon and ambassador -- the ambassador of the European observers and advisor for civilian affairs, flew to Metkovic by helicopter from where the Spanish Battalion was to escort them to Mostar. Tell us, did you know that in the evening of the 11th General Petkovic arrived in the area of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that he arrived in the area of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page of this document. On the 12th of May, according to this document, in the headquarters of the Spanish Battalion, an agreement was reached between Petkovic and Halilovic in the presence of General Morillon and Ambassador Thebault on behalf of the European observers. So let's look at the next document, P2344. This is an agreement reached on the 12th of May and signed by Halilovic and Petkovic. It's the agreement mentioned in the Spanish Battalion's report which we saw earlier. My question for you, Mr. Jasak, is as follows: Did you know that on the 12th of May a cease-fire agreement had been reached in detail?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that an agreement on the cessation of hostilities had been signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the situation in Mostar soon change as regards the intensity of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation changed, and there was only sporadic activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, did you have any knowledge to the effect that a large group of people have gathered at the Velez stadium on the 9th of May and that later on these people were taken to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that in the late evening from a television news programme.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From the building of the Main Staff, are you able to see the Velez stadium?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you try to establish why these people were rounded up and taken to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those of us who were sitting in the Main Staff commented on this. I was told that they had learned from colleagues from the operations zone that these were people who had been taken from the areas where there were military activities going on, to shelter them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, in this courtroom we saw evidence that the vast majority of these people were of Muslim ethnicity. Could you explain to us why there was such a disproportionately large number of Muslims among these people compared to the composition of the population at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll try. In my opinion the only possible explanation is that a large number of Croats had already moved out of that part of town. They had taken their children to continue their schooling elsewhere. And a large part of the inhabitants of Mostar came from the surrounding municipalities, and they may have gone away for the weekend. Also, when people heard shells falling, they left the town in their own vehicles. I don't know what else could be the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'll now put a question to you as a resident of Mostar. Do you have any knowledge that in the vicinity of the Velez stadium there was a facility where a large number of buses could be parked?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that near the Velez stadium there was a garage. It belonged to a publicly owned company, Autoprevoz Mostar. As early as April 1992, we had requisitioned their taxis, because that company also had taxis. It was a public transport company.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, I don't intend to continue putting questions on the events of the 9th of May, so if you have any questions about this, please ask them now, because then I would like to discuss events in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one question about the 9th of May. You said that you saw in the headquarters Naletilic. We know that he and his troops participated in some actions and captured Muslims. According to you, in your capacity you're usually informed about the chains of command and the usual military circuits. What about such unit, the Naletilic unit? Could it have acted outside the control of the main -- of the staff? Think about it before you answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as regards the Naletilic unit, if you put such a question hypothetically, it could have taken action without the action of the Main Staff, because I never saw that the Main Staff ever issued them with any tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. One last question, and, again, this is an assumption, and I'm trying to check on these assumptions. Let's imagine that the staff would have decided on the 9th of May to attack the BH Army and that therefore there was some preparation going on before this attack. What about yourself and your boss in the VOS? Would you have been involved in the preparation, in the planning, and in the assessment of the number of forces, friendly forces or enemy forces? I mean, let's not get into the semantic discussion. Besides, would you yourself have worked in the preparation of the plan in light of your functions within the VOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Main Staff, there was no plan whatsoever for any offensive activities. VOS always provided the elements concerning the enemy for any order issued by the Main Staff, and we never provided such elements. So we would have known had the Main Staff been planning anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough. This is an important answer. Remember, you answered under oath, so under -- unless you're lying, but I don't have any elements to prove this. This is what you're saying, and my question is very specific. After four years of trial, I'm now -- I'm putting very focused questions that go to the heart of the problem. So you are telling me that if the HVO had prepared a plan, then you would have been associated inevitably because there was a need to assess enemy troops and that was your job. Therefore, since you were not associated to this, there was no plan drafted by the HVO, and the HVO did not attack on May 9, 1993, in Mostar. This is what you meant; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mrs. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, very briefly, let us try to summarise the situation in Mostar up until the end of June 1993. What would be a general assessment of that period?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aside from sporadic incidents, the situation was quiet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 30th of June, 1993. Does that date bear any special significance for you?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An all-out war with the BH Army broke out in Mostar on that day, war between the BH Army and the HVO. An all-out attack was launched on that day against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were you on duty at the Main Staff the night between the 29th and the 30th of June?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was peculiar about that attack as opposed to earlier attacks, for example, those in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The peculiarity consisted in the fact that the attack came about as a result of treason by Muslim soldiers of the HVO who coordinated this act of treason with the BH Army. It was the most insidious way for something like this to come about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Because of this act of treason was the BH Army able to take or conquer any particular areas?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From East Mostar, further up to the north and Salakovac, specifically the Tihomir Misic Barracks, Vrapcici, Bijelo Polje, as far as Salakovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So following the attack on the 30th of June, who was holding the territory north of Salakovac as far as Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army as well, specifically the forces that headed out from Konjic and Jablanica towards Mostar. On that day, the Konjic-Jablanica-Mostar area was linked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did the VOS have any information at the time indicating the existence of any plans by the BH Army to link up their forces in Mostar and Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VOS did, in fact, have that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What information specifically? Did you include anything in your reports?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our reports we indicated that the BH Army would try to link up these areas, Konjic, Jablanica, and Mostar, in order to obtain the right conditions for pressing on towards Stolac, Capljina, and Neum.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was there a particular date that you envisaged as the date on which this attack could occur?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about the 1st of July, as a matter of fact, in one of our reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, I'm listening to all these details while looking at the map. You're saying that the plan went Konjic, Jablanica, Mostar, all the way to Neum. I'm looking at the map, and I say if this plan had succeeded, the HVO would have been destroyed. Yes or no? Is it true or false?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's true, Your Honour. For the most part, the HVO would have ceased to exist in such areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, what about Mr. Keza, the VOS chief? Did you orally, verbally warn him about the existence of these assessments and predictions?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed that, and I believe that my chief as well spoke to his own superiors. And then the superiors probably discussed this with commanders on the ground. Quite simply, our report was not construed as being particularly alarming; the reason being, local HVO commanders reckoned that after the 9th of May all those who did not wish to remain in the HVO left and that the Muslim members of the HVO who remained were together with the Croats in the HVO from the very beginning and there would be no problems concerning those men.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, did you, at the Main Staff, receive information at one point in time as to how exactly the BH Army established control over the area to the north-east of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received information indicating that there had been an act of treason in Bijelo Polje, and then the -- the stretchers [as interpreted] component worked with the BH Army in order to take this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was there any response, and if so, what kind?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was widespread disappointment and disbelief in the Main Staff, particularly when we heard that three of our own officials of the Main Staff had come to grieve. Bozo Peric's parents, relatives of Tomo Mihalj and Ante Ivankovic [phoen], and, well, you know, those men were with us at the Main Staff. And then we learned at one point that their close relatives had come to grieve. It was a difficult situation to cope with. People simply couldn't understand that the same people with whom they had been sharing food and drinks now started doing things such as these.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you inform General Petkovic of that attack?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Where would General Petkovic normally sleep when he was staying in the Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Grude.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did he come to Mostar immediately, as far as you know, after you informed him?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Petkovic came at about 8.00, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he was before?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been 9.00, actually, and I think he went to the East Herzegovina operation zone just before he came there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know who General Petkovic talked to when he arrived at the Main Staff -- or, rather, did he talk to anyone when he came?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looked quite crestfallen, and I was about to hand over as duty officer, so I -- I wasn't in touch with him after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll be looking at that again later on in terms of what happened to General Petkovic. 4D948 is our next document. It's a set of four that I'm looking at now. It's an order by General Petkovic, dated the 7th of June, 1993. The introduction reads that the order is being adopted because of the Muslim aggression and efforts to establish control over and occupy the Neretva River valley. Can the situation on the ground be based on the reports from the VRS, your own service?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is based on our information. As I said earlier, we were providing this kind of information to the effect that this was a possible development.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The order goes on to say that one must prevent any breakthroughs by the Muslim unit along the Jablanica-Bijelo Polje-Mostar axis. Was that the axis along which they were operating on the 30th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Jablanica-Bijelo Polje-Mostar, and Mostar-Bijelo Polje-Jablanica, and then they met up at Salakovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The order goes on to say that all the lines facing the Muslims must be reinforced by engineering work. One must lay obstacles along the lines and build new positions down the depth. My question: Are these preparations for defensive activities or offensive activities?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, these are defensive activities. When someone is building new positions down the depth, what that means is they're preparing for the eventuality that all the other positions further up front might fall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: 4D702. 4D702. A letter by General Petkovic on the 30th of June, dispatched to Wahlgren and Morillon. Paragraph 5 states that the HVO and the Croatian people would defend. Nevertheless, it also says that this would not be possible without a great amount of sacrifice on the part of the Muslim forces. Could you, therefore, please caution the commanders of the so-called BH Army about these consequences and call upon them to immediately cease-fire. Mr. Jasak, could you please comment on this appeal made by General Petkovic to the international forces? He was asking them to mediate and try to and broker a cease-fire; right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure I can comment on that. This was an appeal or a call by General Petkovic for the international community to get involved in order to keep large-scale civilian casualties from occurring and in order to help stop the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Given the fact you knew General Petkovic personally and you actually saw him only the 30th of June, could you tell us, in your opinion, this call on the international community to mediate, would you take that to be an earnest endeavour by General Petkovic to stop a large-scale conflict from erupting?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knowing General Petkovic, before and after, I can tell you that what he was doing was always very sincere.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next document, 2D448.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, document 4D702 is important as far as I'm concern. It is written by General Petkovic, but it is sent to the highest international authorities, General Wahlgren and General Morillon. On reading this document, it's obvious -- when reading the document, the ABiH attacked. So the following question springs to mind: Is General Petkovic just making fun of the international community and saying things that are not true? Could he actually try to -- to make -- to talk to these authorities and not tell them the truth? He is mentioning a meeting that he had with General Morillon in Medjugorje on July 26th -- on June 26th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- four days earlier when he told us -- told him that there was a possibility that the Muslim side could attack, and he is calling on the international community to put an end to this. Now, you were on the ground at the time. Could you tell us whether this document perfectly reflects what you experienced in the field or whether there are some elements that could be challenged? And in such a case, could you tell us which elements could be challenged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document is completely identical to my own memory of that period. More so, since this is mentioned here: "We would like to remind you that our side, during the meeting with General Morillon in Medjugorje, on the 26th of June, 1993, warned everyone there about the possibility that there was a plan for a frontal attack by the Muslim forces against Mostar and HVO positions and its surroundings." This was exactly along the same lines as the sort of information that the VOS kept forwarding to General Petkovic. He obviously presented this information to the international community, specifically to General Morillon, on 26th of June, 1993. And this is perfectly consistent with the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question, but it will depend on the knowledge that you have. At the time, not now but at the time, had you followed closely the international negotiations held in Geneva which aim at restoring peace between all sides and setting up a system that would make it possible for all ethnicities to live together peacefully and, you know, which led to the Vance-Owen Plan and so on. Were you aware of all the efforts employed by the international community to try and find -- to strike the right balance between the Serbs, the Muslims, and the Croats, all three communities?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, anyone in that area was following these developments, and the same applied to us who were with the VOS, with a great deal of interest. It was something that everyone over there cared about the most, to have peace back as soon as possible and for the clashes to end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're saying that at VOS you were following this, but given this, in this document that we have here, there is mention of the possibility that Muslims want to have an access to the sea. Does this motivation, obtaining an access to the sea, could it destroy the very fragile balance that the international community was trying to strike, as long as this problem of access to sea wasn't solved? So with this in mind, the BH Army could have thought, Well, we want to have an access to the sea; we will have our access to the sea; and then the international community will have to live with that. Had this been integrated into the work done by the VOS? Had the VOS taken that into account in it's work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the question is maybe a little too broad. I'm not sure I understand the question in its entirety. Are we talking about our assessments in which we tried to show that the BH Army had every intention of starting out from Konjic-Jablanica-Mostar and then eventually reaching the sea coast? Is that what we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You say that the question had been dealt with, if I understand you well. But if the BH Army actually reached the sea, the coast, you answered earlier, but could you be more specific? Could you tell us what the consequences of this would be for you, for the Croats, living in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only talk about the military component. The Croats and the HVO would have vanished from the area as far as any military activity was concerned. I'm not talking about anything that is political.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, would it have made any difference if, for example, the Muslim side in Bosnia-Herzegovina was granted a piece of territory near the sea coast? And on the other hand, the following situation: The BH Army takes such territory by force. Would that have made any difference in terms of the non-Muslim population in that area? Would people be leaving on a massive scale if they had been fighting in that area? I'm just trying to talk about two very hypothetical situations.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thing is if you take something by force and the other is if something is actually peacefully agreed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So what it's difference?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there's agreement, this is a peaceful method of implementing something, no problem there. If you take the military avenue, then you have a problem because you drive out the other ethnic group that is there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll skip Arif Pasalic's speech and try to focus on the following document, 2D1389, a report by the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The date is the 30th of June, 1993, specifically the paragraph that refers to the 4th Corps. Let's keep the part where they say that the Ustashas were the first to attack and then the BH Army launched a counter-attack, as they call it, and then what do they take, it reads: Sjeverni Logor, Rastani, Vrapcici, Bijelo Polje, Salakovac, and Rosici [phoen]. Aside from that, the BH Army is holding all the hydroelectric power plants along the Neretva River with the exception of the one at Capljina. Mr. Jasak, according to your information as far as the facts of this report are concerned about the locations that were taken, would that strike you as accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report on the locations that were taken is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The last sentence says that the 4th and the 6th Corps linked up. Does that mean that East Mostar and Jablanica linked up to all practical intents?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that East Mostar, Konjic, and Jablanica linked up. Jablanica, Konjic, Mostar, all together. The 6th Corps was from Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's in relation to this period; right, because a month and a half before it was very different; right? It was in late June, the 6th Corps for Konjic and Jablanica; right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The 6th Corps was created by taking a component of the 2nd corps; right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to my colleagues for these leading questions, but I think these facts are well established in this trial. P3030.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, too bad that Ms. West is not here. But had she been here, she would have been interested in my question. Now this document establishes that on the 30th of June there is link-up between the 4th and the 6th Corps. That is what is stated here, black and white. And this is not an HVO document; this is the document from the BH Army. Does this mean that a Muslim from East Mostar, because of this link-up, could leave Mostar and go to Jablanica without any difficulty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, they could leave. The only difficulty was the fighting going on, but the possibility was certainly there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We'll be dealing with that if we can later on. Let us look at the following document: P3030.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on, Mrs. Alaburic. You have 28 minutes left. I see that we still have a lot of documents on the list. Can you please try to sort them by order of importance, because, you know, time flies. And 20 minutes is a very short period of time, unfortunately. Especially, I mean, if some documents have already been admitted, maybe it's better to talk about those which have not yet been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to ask a question with regard to the last document. Perhaps you will not know the answer. That would not be surprising and nothing wrong with it. The very last sentence of the document in English reads: "A captured officer of the HV congratulated our commanders on the exceptional success by our forces." Do you have an idea where this officer of the Croatian Army came from, how it is to be explained that in this action the ABiH, according to what they state, caught an officer of the Croatian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall try to explain. To the best of my knowledge, in Bijelo Polje there were a few officers of the Croatian Army who had come as volunteers to help the Croats and the Muslims in the organisation of the defence from the Army of Republika Srpska. It is possible that it's one of those officers maybe. I know of two or three of them who originally hailed from that area. That is to say that at that time they were in the first barracks in Bijelo Polje, that was 50 per cent Muslim, and together with -- so, rather, it was the HVO, the Croats and Muslims together within the HVO that took part in defence against the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, tell us, now since His Honour Judge Trechsel drew our attention to this last part of the report, if we look at the conclusions, relations with the HVO, what is referred to is the exceptional success of the 4th and 6th Corps, this action to the north of East Mostar, and it says that a large part of the territory was liberated, important facilities, and all of that in one day only. Tell me, are these actually the events that we've been speaking of up until now?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It is precisely those events.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next document, P3030. Can you tell us what this document is and whether you've known it before as well.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know this document from before. It is an interim report of one of our interception groups. And at 20 minutes past 1500 hours, they intercepted a conversation between Arif Pasalic and Sefer Halilovic. Over here on the right you can see that as soon as the document arrived, I immediately copied it to three addresses, Bruno, Petkovic, Keza. That's what I put up here. So it end up -- ended up with the head of the defence department, the head of the Main Staff, and we at the VOS kept a copy. And that is why it is here as such. It is not processed. It is not in the VOS report because it was something that had to be sent further on as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We see from this document that Halilovic is congratulating Pasalic on his success. Also, they are stating that they will soon meet up in Salakovac. Tell us, how could Halilovic reach Salakovac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could get there --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From what direction?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He'd get out to Sarajevo, Konjic, Jablanica, Salakovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: How can Pasalic get to Salakovac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salakovac, Mostar, Vrapcici, Bijelo Polje, Salakovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is that further confirmation that Jablanica and East Mostar were linked up?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Had they not been linked up, they could not be meeting at Salakovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Further on it says in the conversation there can be no stopping while there is a single Ustasha left. Can you give us your comment on that sentence?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means practically that the area should be cleansed of all Croats, because at that time they treated all Croats as Ustashas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hear my colleagues moaning for a break, so perhaps it would be the right moment to take one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's take a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, let's look at the next document in this set of documents, 4D480. This is a report of General Petkovic to the Defence Department about what happened on the 30th of June. Inter alia -- actually, can you tell us for starters --

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what document did you say?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was signed by General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise General Petkovic's signature with certainty?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: This document says that the main task is to prevent the link-up of Muslim forces of Jablanica and Mostar. Can you explain to us, Mr. Jasak, how is it that General Petkovic is writing this, namely to prevent what we saw the BH Army report say a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document that was written sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So combat activities continued, and at the end of the day the report was different. Is that what you're -- is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. This was before the 4th and 6th Corps had linked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document it also says that in the area of Bijelo Polje the balance of forces is 60:40 per cent in favour of the Muslims and the population ratio is 80:20, again, in favour of the Muslims. To the best of your knowledge are these figures right, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, these figures are sort of around that. I thought it was 50:50, but I note there were more than 50 per cent Muslims in the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When General Petkovic says 60:40 in favour of the Muslims, would that be the structure of HVO units in the area of Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That would be the structure in the area of Bijelo Polje. That is to say, if we take this battalion of Bijelo Polje into account, that was over 50 per cent Muslim, and then a bit further down to the south there was part of the 2nd Battalion, practically an entire company was purely Muslim. Then this structure of 60:40 per cent I think is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to deal with the Muslims in the HVO in a bit more detail. Tell us, did some services in Herceg-Bosna believe that a high percentage of Muslim soldiers in the HVO could constitute a security threat?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, that was assumed by the services.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what services?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military and civilian, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look a few -- at a few documents in the next set of documents. I am skipping eight documents, so can we please look at document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question to the witness, if I may. Witness, when we look at the document 4D480, when he talks about the Muslim soldiers which have attacked the HVO soldiers at 3.00 a.m., as a military intelligence officer, were there foreboding signs of this attack? And if that is the case, what were the measures which you took accordingly to face the attack, in particular to inform the HVO authorities? And if it had not been the case, how can you explain this shortcoming? How come you were not able to see or -- that the situation would arise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we had envisaged this kind of situation. I said that in one of my answers a few moments ago. In our report of the VOS, and I remember having personally signed it because it was in the late afternoon hours because the chief of VOS was not there, I actually wrote that a day before this. However, our assessment was that this could escalate most probably on the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, in your reports did you envisage that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina could take some territories due to the betrayal of Muslim -- Muslim soldiers in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did envisage such possibilities. However -- well, I mean that that could happen in the area of Mostar and further south, further to the south of Mostar. However, commanders believed those persons who had stayed on in these units after the 9th of May, and they said, "Oh, no. There's not going to be a conflict, because we waged war together with them against the Serbs all the time." I think that, therefore, the Main Staff did not react in a different way either.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say that commanders believed or trusted the people who stayed on with them after the 9th of May, tell us precisely who was it that they trusted?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They trusted the HVO soldiers who were of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us look a few documents now. The first one will be P1438. This is a report on the situation in the 1st Brigade of the HVO. February 1993 is the date. Do you remember, Mr. Jasak, that information about the ethnic structure of the 1st Brigade in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. The 1st Brigade had about 1600 members who were ethnic Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the percentage was?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was somewhat over 35 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this report, towards the very end when assessing the situation, it says the security of defence is down because of a considerable number of Muslims in the unit, over 50 per cent. To the best of your knowledge, Mr. Jasak, after this report did anything change in the behaviour of the military authorities towards the Muslim soldiers of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge nothing had changed, because we held the front lines against the Army of Republika Srpska together.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document, 2D1379. This is a report of the SIS for the first half of 1993. In the fifth section, roughly around the middle, it says: "As a special problem with regard to certain units, we pointed out the large number of soldiers who were of non-Croat ethnicity, mostly Muslims. The importance of this warning was particularly confirmed and came to the fore during the recent conflict in Bijelo Polje when the soldiers of the HVO of Muslim ethnicity crossed over to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and were the strongest Muslim unit, and also in the attack on Gubavica and Dubravska Visoravan." Mr. Jasak, you said that together with the SIS and other security services you exchanged information. Were you in the VOS aware of this position taken by the SIS because of the large number of Muslim soldiers in HVO units?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer, I think that as you read this out in the -- as you read this out I think that you made a mistake. The recent attack of the army against the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. If I made a mistake, then that's it. Could you please go on.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is knowledge that we had in the service and we showed through all those reports. However, I would like to underline once again that commanders simply could not accept the possibility of any such thing ever happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Jasak, did you have any kind of knowledge to the effect that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina would systemically work against -- work vis-à-vis the Muslim soldiers in the HVO and count on them as an auxiliary force in some of the conflicts in the territories that up until then had been under HVO control?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: VOS had knowledge to that effect, that members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were meeting up, I mean Muslims, with members of the Croatian Defence Council who were also Muslims. There was some information to the effect that they were trying to recruit people who were of Muslim ethnicity and who were in the HVO. Namely, they wanted them to stay on in their respective units up until a point when they would be called. So there were pressures that were exerted against the families of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, I would just like to check now whether I understood you correctly. Are you trying to tell us that some soldiers of Muslim ethnicity stayed in the HVO in agreement with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that then at a certain point in time the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina would call them to participate in some activities against the HVO? Is that what you were trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what I said, that they should stay in the HVO until they're called, because by then they would have been trained soldiers with weapons and they could carry out any task that had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now have a look at the next document, P2562. This is a report of the commander of the 5th Battalion in the 2nd Brigade about the Muslims in that unit. Tell us, the 2nd Brigade operated in the territory to the north of East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this 5th Battalion was from the area of Ilici.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us see what he says about his Muslims. He says: "Probably the high percentage of Muslims who have stayed on in our unit was caused by their position within our populated areas but also by previous activities of our IPD service which held meetings with Muslims and explained the real situation to them." Now I'm skipping a few sentences, and I quote further on: "We believe that the Muslims will stay on in our units but more as an effect of the fact that they live in the area where the majority are Croats." Tell us, Mr. Jasak, this commander, did he want soldiers of Muslim ethnicity who were up until that moment in his unit, and that moment was May 1993? Did he want the Muslims to stay on in that unit or not?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He absolutely wanted them to stay in that unit because they were from that area where that unit was. That is to say, they lived together with the Croats that he referred to, Ilici, Polog, Meljine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next document, 5D1115. 5D1115. That's fine. This is an order of the commander of the 3rd Brigade of the HVO, dated the 28th of May, 1993. So it's the same period. Tell us, the 3rd Brigade, what's the territory that it held, which positions?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the south of East Mostar. South-east, to the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, you told us yesterday that the greatest number of Muslim soldiers who left, left from this brigade, following the clashes on the 9th of May, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Two Muslim battalions left from this unit, taking all of their weapons with them. I think about 800 men. As many as that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What does the commander of this brigade say specifically in paragraph 2? The IPD services of these units and all of the commanders from the detachment level to the uppermost level in that unit are intensifying their relations in terms of settling their mutual relations within that unit with the objective of, among other things, in view of the necessity of continuing to co-exist in this area in which the unit was stationed. And then, among other things, keeping the Muslim members in the units, specifically those who were no extremists and were only thinking about fighting the common enemy. Mr. Jasak, based on this document, could you perhaps tell us what the position was of the 3rd Brigade commander concerning the Muslims in his unit. Was their presence desirable or not?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what we see written here, their presence was desirable, except for the presence of extremists.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the position of the military commanders was as follows: The extremists among the Muslims had probably left the HVO units by this time anyway?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely what I said earlier on during my evidence. All those who, in one way or another, opposed the co-operation between Muslims and Croats abandoned the HVO after the 9th of May. Another thing that is mention here is the necessity of continuing to co-exist, to live side by side in the area in which the unit is stationed. Therefore, no matter what happened next, they would have to get on living together side by side from the next day on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, can you explain the fact that the commander, Primorac, here orders to keep only those Muslims who are not extreme? If all that are extreme had already left, would he then have reason to make that order? It's the last bullet point under number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having learned from previous experiences, meaning this is the unit that got hurt the most in that period. Eight hundred of their Muslim men had left, with about 200 more remaining. Probably no other unit was more severely affected than this one. They had lost a lot of their weapons. They asked for protection and asked to see if there was anything the service could do for them in terms of checking whether any extremists still remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have to use up a minute or two to just clarify something. What exactly is this about? Item 2 or paragraph 2 tells us that the IPD service and the commanders should step up their work with their own men in order to bring the relations within the unit back to normal. And then, among other objectives, they seem to want to keep Muslim men who are no extremists. The conclusion would seem to be, "We will not be trying to hold back the extremists, if any. If they want to leave, they're free to do that." Do you think that interpretation of the order would be accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think the conclusion is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next document, not literally. It's -- there are a number of documents before the ones that we've been looking at. It's 4D1461. 1461. This is an Official Note - please just listen to me - of the Information and Security Service, dated September 1992. A while ago we were talking about the talks to keep some Muslims in the HVO as a result of an agreement with the BH Army. This report states, I quote: "According to certain sources on the 16th of September this year in the evening hours, Muharem Dizdar, one of the HVO commanders, and Ragib Dizdar were visiting Muslim members of the HVO of Islamic faith telling them not to leave their units, the HVO units, and not to join the BH Army until time was ripe. They also said that they would be informing them of that in due course." Mr. Jasak, is that precisely what you were telling us about a while ago, the activities of the BH Army vis-à-vis the Muslim members of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that's just that. It's exactly what I was talking about. They wanted them to stay with the HVO until the moment was right for them to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasak, when, the 30th of June, the Muslim soldiers of the HVO's 2nd Brigade betrayed their fellow soldiers and turned on them during that night, disarming them in the process, what happened in the Mostar area? Were any steps taken to disarm and isolate the Muslim soldiers in that area?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, such steps were taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge indicating that there were military commanders who were involved in taking those decisions and taking those measures?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was one of the most difficult days of their lives. They were aware of what had occurred on the 9th of May. Those who left were those who wanted to leave. Nevertheless, what happened on the 30th of June in Bijelo Polje, they understood that the Muslims in these units were a security issue; but on the other hand, it was also a broad human issue you might say. It was difficult for them to start disarming all these soldiers now whom they had been fighting alongside from the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Final question on this: Had the Muslim soldiers in the units in the Mostar region done the same thing that the Muslims in the 2nd Brigade had done before them, would the Croatian authorities in Herceg-Bosna still have managed to hold on to their control over any part of the South-Eastern Herzegovina operation zone?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They would have been unable to maintain that control.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Jasak. I know that my time is up, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. You have used up the six hours that were allotted to you. The Defence -- the other Defence teams will now have three hours for their cross-examination. Let me ask of all teams how they've allotted the times among themselves. 1D, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning Your Honours, good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. We do not have any questions for the gentleman. We do wish to thank him for coming here to give his evidence, and I did commit my time to the Praljak Defence team in the event they -- they need to go beyond the, I believe, 30 minutes that they are allotted to. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. 2D. Just a minute. 2D.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. The Stojic Defence will be cross-examining the witness. Nevertheless, we only come after 3D, Mr. Praljak's Defence. We're the last to start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, 3D will intervene. Mr. Kovacic, how long do you need? How much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reckon we'll be using up all of our time, at least the 30 minutes allotted to us plus the time so generously granted to us by the Prlic Defence team. With your leave, the first part of the cross-examination will be conducted by General Praljak. We realise, based on the chief, that these are subjects that are closely tied to the army itself, their positions, operations, and developments at the time. You also know very well that General Praljak was there, including his time in the Main Staff at the same time as this witness. Therefore, he has special knowledge. There can be no doubt about that, and direct experience of these developments. And maybe also something to do with Paket radio communications. After that, my learned friend Ms. Pinter would like to examine the witness on a number of documents that directly relate to the topics covered so far. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Our time is precious, so, Mr. Praljak, you might start now. You have -- we have 12 minutes remaining. I believe that 5D -- well, I don't know. Will 5D need time for questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we do not have a definite position at this time. We would like to hold on to our time, but we will be coming after the Praljak Defence, so we'll decide tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's why I didn't put the question to you, but my fellow Judge wanted you to have a [indiscernible]. What about D6?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. General Praljak, you have the floor. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you. Given the short time I have, I will turn this around a little.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jasak.

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, let's start with some minor matters. You are with the Croatian Army, as you said. The Croatian Army is a member of NATO; right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: A brigadier belongs to the general's echelon or is that below in terms of rank?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking of high ranking officers, we have lower ranking officers and high ranking officers. This is the highest rank among the highest ranking officers. The only rank above brigadier is general.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You have a single star on your epaulette, right? Are you, in fact, a brigadier general?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Fine. All right, all right. We've got that clarified now. When you commanded a battalion in Mostar, what rank would that have normally have implied in an army?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major or colonel, depending.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is that a higher rank or a lower rank?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a higher rank.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When you were discharging your duties in the Main Staff as an analyst analysing everything that was going on within the operations zone, which was the rank that belonged to you at the time? I'm not saying you actually held it, because that's a different problem, but in order to exercise that very responsible duty, which rank would that have required?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again the rank of major, but that was absolutely the highest level in that area. Only the chief of service held a higher rank at the time, and we there were receiving all the information from the field. So there was no one above me in terms of rank in the analysis section or department.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right. Let us press on. The year is 1991. In your part of Mostar, did you have any sort of military organisation?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late in 1991, we organised ourselves on a voluntary basis. People had something that was very much like a battalion that they had managed to organise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: How many battalions like that were inside Mostar organised by Croats?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: A total of nine battalions and four independent companies. We tried to organise another one like that but not before 1992 on the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So only one on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Who was the commander of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: No, you will have to repeat the answer. How many battalions or companies did the Muslims have early in 1992 or late in 1991?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late in 1991, not a single one; early in 1992, one battalion. They called it a battalion, but it numbered no more than 150 men.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Who was the commander of your battalion until the day he died?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tihomir Misic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: How did you choose Tihomir Misic to become your commander? Did another commander perhaps come along telling you that you should choose him? Did instructions arrive from Sarajevo from Izetbegovic or whoever? How was Tihomir Misic selected?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a well-regarded and very able person. People trusted him. His ability to organise things was very notable, and the choice was a natural one. It's not that someone put his name forward or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So you just selected him; right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we believed that he was the best among us, and he was the person that everyone trusted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is this how it happened in the other Croat units, too, that were being organised, because it wasn't the HVO as such, not at this stage?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was how the Croats organised themselves in other areas, too, other local communes in the general Mostar area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, could you explain a bit more specifically how this happened? Did the battalion gather and then there was a potation, or did some of the officers decide this, or did someone outside the battalion upon proposal by members decide on this? How -- how was the proceedings for the -- how were the proceedings for this appointment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said a thing or two about that yesterday, and I'll try to provide more detail today. The procedure was like this: Say I was familiar with five or ten people and one of my colleagues was also familiar with five or ten people, and then groups would be set up in local communes, and then people would choose from among themselves. They would simply sit down, talk, and agree on who would become the leader of that group. For example, at the level of the Zahum local commune, Tihomir Misic was chosen to be commander because he was the ablest person around. There were no orders or recommendations or anything like that for that appointment. Once people had realised that the village of Ravno had been burnt to the ground, they started to organise themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You said that in 1991, in addition to the JNA, another two corps arrived in Mostar, but let's not go into that again. Where exactly did the JNA go inside Mostar with those volunteers? Hum?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sjeverni Logor?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Juzni Logor?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The airport?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's press on. Hum?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sjeverni Logor?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Juzni Logor?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The airport?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's not "Luzni" Logor, it's "Juzni" Logor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not "Uzni," "Juzni." Yes, Heliodrom, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Cule?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Fortica?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The repeater on Mount Velez?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tepcici, Slipcici, near Citluk?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they held that area, too, under their control. They were present in the area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tepcici, Slipcici, were they there too?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were there too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did they have a full military control of Mostar from all sides as well as Mostar's broader surroundings?

utterances.speaker: RADMILO JASAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostar was entirely under their control, as well's as its surroundings, with the exception of one way out towards Goranci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, we will stop now and, of course, you'll continue tomorrow. But it's time to stop. Sir, please some back tomorrow at 2.15 p.m. and until then, of course, do not contact anyone, according to what I told you earlier. Tomorrow we'll only break once for 20 minutes and we'll stop around 6.00 p.m. If we're not finished tomorrow, we will continue next Monday for the cross-examination of the other Defences, and the Prosecutor will start its own cross-examination next week as planned. Thank you.
